correctness.rationale: Every missing segment of a geodesic polygon side admits an internally disjoint alternate subarc in its connected complement. Such pairs form one of the three theta cycles, yielding an exhaustive one-arm, both-poles, or one-pole classification. Shortest-path inequalities bound all cases. The exact metric distance maximum in the one-pole case is (max(u,v)+min(u,v,K))/2; the explicit geodesic witness with u=(c+a)/2, v=min(a,(b−a)/2) attains (c+min(b,3a))/4. Boundary a=b and b=3a checked. The standalone exact-mesh enumerator passed 3,128 path-pair checks on seven test meshes and 252 rational witness checks; the continuum proof does not rely on them.

value.rationale: The minimal network of three competing routes is a natural test object for quantitative tree-likeness. The answer is sharp for every positive real choice of arm lengths and every polygon size, with a geometrically nontrivial screening transition at b=3a: beyond that threshold increasing the middle-arm length does not change the invariant. This is a complete structural metric classification, distinct from established four-point or triangle invariants.
